newsitem.title: POLAND: EARLY ZLOTY SLIPS VS BASKET, 1-DAY RATES RISE.
newsitem.headline: EARLY ZLOTY SLIPS VS BASKET, 1-DAY RATES RISE.

text.p: The zloty eased against its currency basket in early Thursday trade as Polish banks rebuilt foreign currency positions after slightly shortening them on Wednesday, dealers said.
They said the zloty would continue to follow dollar/mark shifts and stay around minus one percent from the parity rate.
"The zloty will not ease significantly below -1.0 percent because this level satisfies both the central bank and players," said Dorota Alender, forex dealer at bank BIG SA.
At 0915 GMT the zloty was at -1.07/-1.13 percent from the trading band centre against -0.81/-0.95 percent at opening.
It was at 3.5090/10 to the dollar and at 1.8665/75 to the mark against opening's 3.5050/00 and 1.8580/05 respectively.
Dealers said foreign investors were largely absent from the market, only occasionly checking rates and market sentiment.
"No major foreign capital inflows should be expected before parliamentary elections in late September," said Andrzej Fiderkiewicz, dealer at Societe Generale in Warsaw.

"If the present leftist coalition wins the elections, which is quite likely despite the recent flood crisis, foreigners should come back," he added. Recent opinion polls put the ex-communist SLD just ahead of the right-wing Solidarity group.
Foreign economists have said they preferred a SLD victory because the ex-communists were already tested by the markets, unlike the Solidarity trade union-led opposition group.
Overnight deposits inched up to around 23.25 percent at offer from opening's 23.10 and dealers expected one-day cash to remain between 23-23.5 percent in the near-term.

"After the interest rate rise the level of 23 percent should hold for some time...likely until banks have to square required reserves at the end of the month," said Piotr Schmidt of Pekao SA. Tomorrow/next rose to 22.95/23.47 from 22.80/23.30
